accepted_limitations: M1 evaluates the scalar Stokes I field only; MModeSimulator.supports_polarization is False and non-zero Q, U, or V is rejected with issue code mmode_m1_scalar_only until phase M2 is accepted.

M1's E (primary beam) term is the accepted project-wide scalar model (E = e * I2, an analytic circular-aperture Gaussian-tapered response); no beam squint or full-efield vector physics is exercised by this fixture.

No GPU or other accelerator run of the m-mode solver has been measured; PERF-001 remains open and the M3 performance record (not yet reached) is the only venue that could license a speed or accelerator claim.

The Section 7.3 transfer-sample concatenation vectors are not embedded per-direction, only their concatenation_sha256 digests, per Section 7.3's second deliberate replay-deferral ruling; this reviewer independently regenerated all 288 rows by directly invoking the tracked transfer_sample_rows() function twice (confirming determinism) and confirmed every concatenation_sha256 matches exactly.

The full ~16.8 million row operational horizon-scan terminal-cell array is not embedded in the evidence artifact, only its streamed SHA-256, its scan_crossing/guard_interval/excluded_upper_endpoint rows, and one per-direction summary row per Section 12.1's deliberate replay-deferral ruling; this reviewer independently regenerated the complete array by a full replay of the tracked S1 pipeline and confirmed horizon_scan_ledger_sha256 matches exactly (isolation_interval_count = 16,835,749).

The site's geodetic longitude/latitude/height that reach build_frozen_frame differ from the fixture's literal YAML-style values at the sub-ULP / sub-nanometre level because instrument-location resolution round-trips the site through EarthLocation.from_geodetic -> ITRS xyz -> geodetic extraction; this is a deterministic, fully reproducible architectural detail (confirmed by instrumenting the real call site) rather than a defect, but it means a naive direct call to build_frozen_frame with the literal fixture floats does not reproduce the recorded site_sha256/frame_matrix_sha256, which briefly looked like a reproducibility failure during this review before being traced to its source.

rederived_oracles.method: Independently reimplemented Section 3.1's exact-turn ERA grid (N=49, integration_fraction=1) from scratch using Python fractions.Fraction (centers, lower/upper edges, exposure_width, horizon_lo/hi), recomputed all four exact-turn array digests, all three derived-radian array digests (via one final round-to-nearest of exact(tau)*rational, matching round_to_nearest_turn_radians), and the combined canonical_era_grid_sha256 -- all matched the retained evidence bit-for-bit. Independently confirmed horizon_hi-horizon_lo==1 exactly (Fraction arithmetic) while also computing the rounded-radian view of that same subtraction and showing the design does not rely on that rounded equality as its closure predicate (Section 3.1's explicit distinction). Separately reproduced era_center_max_residual_rad and era_step_max_residual_rad end-to-end by running the actual tracked S1 generator/solver pipeline (build_frozen_frame + build_canonical_era_grid via a fresh Simulator.from_mapping(...).setup().run() in the exact recorded environment) and confirmed canonical_era_grid_sha256 and canonical_era_turn_grid_sha256 reproduce bit-for-bit against the retained certificate.

Independently computed xp0_arcsec/yp0_arcsec from the installed bundled astropy_iers_data finals2000A.all table via table.pm_xy(anchor) (public astropy IERS_A API), converted to radians via erfa.DAS2R, and computed sp0_rad via erfa.sp00 and RPOM0 via erfa.pom00 -- all called directly, independent of radiosim.core.mmode.frame. Initial direct comparison against the retained frame_matrix_manifest showed the geodetic longitude/latitude/height literals from the YAML-like fixture are NOT what reaches build_frozen_frame verbatim: instrument-location resolution round-trips the site through EarthLocation.from_geodetic -> ITRS xyz -> .lon/.lat/.height, perturbing latitude from -30.72152 to -30.721519999999995 and height from 1073.0 to 1073.00000000035 at the sub-ULP/sub-nanometre level (a real, deterministic, and fully reproducible architectural detail, not a bug -- confirmed by instrumenting the actual production call site and by re-running the resolution twice). Once the correctly resolved geodetic values were used, xp0_arcsec, yp0_arcsec, das2r_rad_per_arcsec, xp0_rad, yp0_rad, sp0_rad and the resulting site_sha256/frame_matrix_sha256 all reproduced bit-for-bit against the retained evidence, confirmed both by direct erfa/astropy recomputation and by a full independent replay of the tracked S1 pipeline.

Algebraically re-derived Section 12.1's closed-form A = g1*c1+g2*c2, B = g1*c2-g2*c1, C = g3*c3 from first principles, starting from sin(alt(u)) = (T(0) R3(alpha) c) . up = c^T R3(alpha)^T g with g = T(0)^T up and R3(alpha)^T = R3(-alpha), expanding the passive_r3 matrix by hand and matching the code's formula exactly. Independently recomputed era0_rad via erfa.era00(*ut1_two_part), RPOM0 via erfa.pom00, and T(0) = RPOM0 @ R3(era0_rad) via direct matrix multiplication using my own passive_r3 implementation; all matched the retained frame_matrix_manifest bit-for-bit (after correcting for the geodetic round-trip noted under m1.polar-motion-unit-path). Verified both RPOM0 and the composed anchor matrix are orthonormal (R R^T - I) and proper (det=+1), and verified erfa.era00 increases monotonically with UT1 (rigid eastward rotation sign sanity).

Wrote an independent implementation (not calling frame_mod._transport_tangent_frame) of the Section 4.1 Richardson-extrapolated North/East tangent Jacobian for the M1 point source (ICRS ra=0deg, dec=-75deg): built eight probe unit vectors displaced by +/-2**-12 and +/-2**-13 rad along catalogue North/East, transformed all of them through the public astropy SkyCoord(CartesianRepresentation).transform_to(CIRS(obstime=t0)) API, formed the coarse and fine central differences, Richardson-combined them, projected off the radial direction, Gram-Schmidt-orthogonalized East against North, and checked the declared handedness dot(cross(N,E),c) < 0. Independently confirmed orthonormality (N.N, E.E ~= 1; N.E, N.c, E.c ~= 0 to within 1e-16..1e-23) and the required negative handedness.

Independently coded Section 12.1's exhaustive topology decision (rho2=A^2+B^2, the five exhaustive cases) from the memo text, fed it the A,B,C computed above for (a) the M1 point source and (b) one transfer-grid direction (transfer_quadrature:production:8:128) drawn from the retained evidence's scan_crossing rows purely to pick a nontrivial example to test (not to validate against). For (a) the analytic solver returned 'circumpolar_no_root'; independently sampled sin(alt) at 12 evenly spaced turns across the full cycle via a from-scratch call to astropy SkyCoord.transform_to(AltAz(obstime=...,location=...,pressure=0)) (bypassing the frozen model and the scan entirely) and confirmed every sample strictly positive (min 0.2689), confirming the no-root classification directly against the public operational trajectory. For (b) the analytic solver returned two transverse roots at turns 0.5732 and 0.7490; independently probed sin(alt) via the same direct AltAz calls at +/-1e-6 turn around each solved root and confirmed a genuine sign change at both, confirming the closed-form roots coincide with true zero-crossings of the independently sampled operational trajectory.

Independently computed exp(+i*2*pi*m*u) via Python's cmath for m in {-2,-1,0,1,2} at three exact turns (1/8, 3/7, 5/5) and compared against radiosim.core.mmode.time.unit_circle_turn(m*u) (the module's correctly-rounded unit-circle kernel), confirming the sign convention (positive m advances phase, exp(+i*2*pi*m*u), matching Section 6's stated K/DFT sign) and that all 15 residuals sit at machine precision.
